title: A carried-over batch is offered next session
asA: operator whose session ended before the ask fired
iWant: the SessionEnd hook to flush a bundle idempotently and the SessionStart hook of the next session to inject a one-line context reminder that pending entries exist
soThat: a crash or /clear does not lose findings and the next session's first pause carries the ask

acceptanceCriteria.description: rcf feedback hook session-end writes the outbox bundle for any pending entries under 1 second (the shared Claude Code SessionEnd budget is 1.5s) and is byte-idempotent (same content hash means no rewrite). Codex SessionEnd runs the same handler; output is discarded either way. Two bundles it writes in the same second for different pending sets are both kept: neither overwrites the other, and each one's bytes are in exactly one file of the outbox.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a fixture with two pending entries and a stubbed clock so the elapsed time is measurable; for the same-second case, the clock stubbed to one second while a further pending entry is recorded between two runs
acceptanceCriteria.when: rcf feedback hook session-end is run twice back-to-back; for the same-second case, rcf feedback hook session-end is run, a further pending entry is recorded, and it is run again in the same second
acceptanceCriteria.then: the first run writes one bundle file under outbox; the second run runs to completion in under 1 second without rewriting the same-hash file; both exit 0; in the same-second case both bundles are kept, neither overwriting the other, each one's bytes in exactly one file of the outbox

acceptanceCriteria.description: rcf feedback hook session-start with pending entries and a new sessionId prints one plain line to stdout on Claude Code ("rcf feedback: <n> unsubmitted entr(y|ies) carried over from an earlier session; ask the operator once at a natural pause (RULE 17).") and the Codex-shaped equivalent under --harness codex. The line is what the harness injects as context; it never blocks. If SessionStart on Codex cannot inject context (verified at build time against the current Codex reference), the fallback in RULE 17 ("check rcf feedback status at session start") is what carries the same posture.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a fixture with two pending entries carried over from a prior sessionId
acceptanceCriteria.when: rcf feedback hook session-start is run under each harness
acceptanceCriteria.then: the Claude Code stdout matches the exact wording above; the Codex JSON matches the reference shape currently accepted for SessionStart context; both return exit 0; state.json is not mutated (asked is set on Stop, not on session-start)

acceptanceCriteria.description: rcf feedback defer means "not now, ask again next session" (design 3.1). Entries in status deferredUntilSession whose stored sessionId is not the current one are requeued to pending on the SessionStart hook AND on the Stop hook (belt to the SessionStart braces, so the flow works when only Stop is installed). The requeue appends one state-transition line per entry with status pending and no sessionId field, so fold-by-id preserves the entry's prior sessionId and the carry-over gate in both hooks (pending.sessionId !== currentSessionId) fires naturally in the new session. Entries recorded or last deferred under the current sessionId are not re-transitioned (idempotent per session; deferring twice in one session is a no-op on the second call).
acceptanceCriteria.given: a fixture with one pending entry deferred in session A (entries.jsonl carries the deferredUntilSession line with sessionId A)
acceptanceCriteria.when: rcf feedback hook session-start --harness claude-code is run with session_id B, then rcf feedback hook stop --harness claude-code is run with the same session_id B
acceptanceCriteria.then: SessionStart appends one { status: pending } transition (no sessionId field) so the entry returns to pending with its sessionId still A; the carry-over line prints to stdout naming the count and RULE 17; the following Stop exits 2 with the ask on stderr and appends exactly one asked record for session B; a second SessionStart in session B is a no-op (no new transition, silent stdout); a further SessionStart in a fresh session_id C after a Stop-only path (no SessionStart wired) still requeues on the Stop hook so the ask fires there

acceptanceCriteria.description: [must-not] A feedback entry recorded in a linked git worktree is never lost with the worktree and never left where the main checkout would commit it. The queue of a linked worktree lives in the main checkout's .rcf/feedback/ (the round 1 storage choice). An entry rcf feedback add records in a linked worktree is offered from the main checkout after git worktree remove. A queue the worktree already holds in its own .rcf/feedback/ (as 0.36.0 left it) is moved into the main checkout's store by the next rcf feedback command run in the worktree (any sub-verb, the Stop, SessionEnd and SessionStart hooks included) once the main checkout's .gitignore covers .rcf/feedback/, so no entry, old or new, is lost when the worktree is removed, and each keeps its id (listed once) and its status. While the main checkout does not ignore .rcf/feedback/, nothing moves: rcf feedback list and the hooks in that worktree keep reading its own held queue (the Stop hook keeps asking about its pending entries), and rcf feedback add there without --force exits 2, stderr naming .rcf/feedback, rcf doctor --fix and the main checkout's directory and saying "the held entries move into the main checkout once it ignores .rcf/feedback/", and writes nothing under either checkout's .rcf/feedback/; once the main checkout ignores the store, the next rcf feedback command in the worktree moves the held queue as above. If the move fails (for example the main checkout's .rcf/ or a file the move writes there is not writable, or a held file cannot be removed from the worktree), the command exits 1 with stderr naming the error the move hit and the main checkout's directory, and nothing is written to the worktree's queue; the failed move loses nothing and duplicates nothing: every entry the worktree held stays readable from the worktree or the main checkout, a held file is removed only after its content is present in the main store, and the next rcf feedback command run in the worktree, once what made the move fail is put right, completes the move with each id once. Commands that run at the same time change none of this: when two or more rcf feedback commands run in the worktree at once (or in two linked worktrees of one main checkout, each moving its own held queue), or rcf feedback add, a hook or rcf feedback submit writes to the main checkout's store while the move runs, each entry line, ask record and outbox bundle the worktree held lands in the main checkout's store exactly once (never duplicated, overwritten or lost), and an entry or outbox bundle written while the move runs is kept (a bundle in exactly one file of the main checkout's outbox). The main checkout's own ask records are kept the same way: every ask record the main checkout's state.json held before the move, and every ask record its Stop hook writes while the move runs, is in it exactly once afterwards, and a command that reads the main checkout's state.json while another command writes it reads a whole document (a Stop hook in a session that already asked stays silent). A command that reads the main checkout's entries.jsonl while another command writes it (rcf feedback add recording an entry, or a command recording an entry's new status) reads only whole lines, never a partial one. A command that writes to the main checkout's store (rcf feedback add, the Stop hook, the SessionEnd hook or rcf feedback submit) while a move is still changing that store waits for the move for up to 10 seconds; if the move is still running then, the writer exits 1 with stderr naming the running command's process id and the main checkout's directory, and writes nothing under the main checkout's .rcf/feedback/. A move whose process stopped without finishing (no longer running on this host), or that has not been refreshed for 60 seconds, holds up no later command: the next command proceeds, and the next rcf feedback command run in the worktree completes the move with each id once. A move still running is refreshed at least every 5 seconds while it works, so it is never taken for stopped however long ago it started: a writer waiting on it exits 1 as above once its wait runs out. When two or more commands find the same stopped move at once, exactly one of them goes on at any instant: every other writer waits as above and every other move leaves its held queue for a later command, no command sets aside a command still running or one that went on after the stopped move, and each entry line, ask record and outbox bundle any of them writes is in the main checkout's store exactly once. A command that holds the main checkout's store and is judged stopped by a later command while it still runs (it was held up for more than 60 seconds, or its clock is behind the later command's) writes nothing more to the main checkout's store once the later command has taken the store over: it exits 1 with stderr naming the path of the record of its hold that it lost, and every write the later command made is kept. A command that stopped (no longer running on this host) while it was taking over a stopped move holds up no later command either, and the command that goes on past it removes the claim it left in the main checkout's store. A command's record in the main checkout's store that cannot be read (its file cannot be parsed) is judged by that file's age: it holds up no later command once the file is more than 60 seconds old, and a writer it holds up past its wait exits 1 and writes nothing under the main checkout's .rcf/feedback/, with stderr naming that file's path and its age in seconds. The write with which rcf feedback submit records an issue or comment it has already filed is never abandoned on a busy store: it waits for up to 65 seconds by its clock, so a move that stopped refreshing is judged stopped within it and the record lands; if it still cannot write then, submit exits 1 with stderr naming the filed issue's URL and the entry's id, never saying it wrote nothing, and the next rcf feedback submit does not file that entry again. This holds in a linked worktree too: a filing that rcf feedback submit run in the worktree could not record while the worktree kept its own held queue (the main checkout's .gitignore did not cover .rcf/feedback/ yet) moves into the main checkout's store with that queue, exactly once, so the next rcf feedback submit in either checkout does not file that entry again and no held file is left under the worktree's .rcf/feedback/. Whenever rcf feedback submit has already filed or recorded anything (an issue or comment it filed, or a filing an earlier submit kept that it recorded) and a later write of the same run finds the main checkout's store busy past its wait, it exits 1 with stderr naming each entry it filed or recorded by its id and the issue's URL, never saying it wrote nothing. rcf feedback submit --dry-run writes nothing and never lists an entry whose filing an earlier submit kept (filed, not yet recorded) among the entries it would file, comment on or bundle. A Stop hook that does not ask (the operator opted out) and has nothing to write never waits: it exits at once as it would alone. The gitignore pre-write check of rcf feedback add runs against the checkout that holds the store: when the main checkout's .gitignore does not cover .rcf/feedback/, rcf feedback add in the worktree without --force refuses as AC-15501-2 refuses (exit 2, stderr names the missing .rcf/feedback/ entry, rcf doctor --fix and the main checkout's directory) and nothing is created under either checkout's .rcf/feedback/. When the main checkout does not hold the rcf project (rcf adopted on the worktree's branch only), rcf feedback add in the worktree never leaves a file the main checkout would commit; keeping the entry in the worktree or refusing is the builder's choice, and that worktree's queue surviving its removal is out of scope. Worktrees of a bare repository and separate-git-dir worktrees are out of scope. AC-15501-1 and AC-15501-2 are unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a git repository holding an rcf project whose .gitignore covers .rcf/feedback/, and a linked worktree made with git worktree add; variants: (2) the worktree already holds a .rcf/feedback/ queue with one pending and one discarded entry, and the main checkout holds one pending entry of its own; (3) the main checkout's .gitignore does not cover .rcf/feedback/ while the worktree branch's .gitignore does; (4) the main checkout does not hold the rcf project, adopted on the worktree branch only; (5) the worktree holds a .rcf/feedback/ queue with one pending and one discarded entry while the main checkout's .gitignore does not cover .rcf/feedback/ and the worktree branch's .gitignore does; (6) the worktree holds that queue, the main checkout's .gitignore covers .rcf/feedback/ and the main checkout's .rcf/ directory is not writable; (7) the worktree holds a .rcf/feedback/ queue as 0.36.0 left it (entries.jsonl with one pending and one discarded entry, a state.json ask ledger and an outbox bundle), the main checkout's .gitignore covers .rcf/feedback/, the main checkout holds one pending entry and a state.json of its own, and the main checkout's .rcf/feedback/state.json is read-only (a move that fails after appending to the main queue); (8) the worktree holds that queue (entries.jsonl, state.json and an outbox bundle), the main checkout's .gitignore covers .rcf/feedback/ and the worktree's .rcf/feedback/outbox/ is read-only (a move that fails after removing some held files); (9) the worktree holds a .rcf/feedback/ queue as 0.36.0 left it (entries.jsonl, a state.json ask ledger and one or more outbox bundles, 300 in one case), the main checkout's .gitignore covers .rcf/feedback/, and a second command runs while the move runs: another rcf feedback command in the worktree (up to eight at once), rcf feedback add in the worktree or in the main checkout, the SessionEnd hook in the worktree, or in the main checkout writing a bundle under a held bundle's name, the Stop hook in the main checkout writing its ask ledger, rcf feedback submit in the main checkout writing a bundle under a held bundle's name, or a second linked worktree of the same main checkout moving a held queue of its own (its SessionEnd bundle under the first worktree's bundle name with other bytes); (10) the worktree holds a .rcf/feedback/ queue as 0.36.0 left it (entries.jsonl, a state.json ask ledger and outbox bundles), the main checkout's .gitignore covers .rcf/feedback/, the main checkout holds pending entries of its own and, in some cases, a state.json ask record, and while a worktree move runs: the main checkout's Stop hook writes its ask ledger between the move's read and its write of the main checkout's state.json; the move reads the main checkout's state.json while the main checkout's Stop hook is writing it; the Stop hook, in a session that already asked, reads it while the move is writing it; rcf feedback add, the Stop hook, the SessionEnd hook and rcf feedback submit run in the main checkout while the move is held past their wait; or the move's process stops without finishing, or started more than 60 seconds before rcf feedback add runs in the main checkout and has not been refreshed since; (11) the worktree holds a .rcf/feedback/ queue as 0.36.0 left it, the main checkout's .gitignore covers .rcf/feedback/, the main checkout holds pending entries of its own, and a worktree move that started more than 60 seconds before rcf feedback add runs in the main checkout is still running and has been refreshed since; (12) the worktree holds a .rcf/feedback/ queue as 0.36.0 left it, the main checkout's .gitignore covers .rcf/feedback/, the main checkout holds pending entries of its own, and: a worktree move's process stopped without finishing and three Stop hooks in the main checkout, each for its own session_id, find it at once and judge it stopped; rcf feedback add, or rcf feedback discard, writes the main checkout's entries.jsonl while rcf feedback list reads it; rcf feedback submit in the main checkout has filed an issue for an entry when a worktree move holds the main checkout's store, and the move then lets the store go, stops refreshing for more than 60 seconds by submit's clock, or holds the store past submit's wait; the operator opted out of the ask (in the feedback settings, or with RCF_FEEDBACK_ASK=0) and the main checkout's Stop hook runs while a worktree move holds the store; or a stopped move's record in the main checkout's store cannot be parsed and rcf feedback add runs in the main checkout when that file is 30, or more than 60, seconds old; (13) the worktree holds a .rcf/feedback/ queue as 0.36.0 left it, the main checkout's .gitignore covers .rcf/feedback/, the main checkout holds pending entries of its own, and: a worktree move's process stopped without finishing, a Stop hook in the main checkout that judged it stopped is still running inside its claim on it, and a second Stop hook whose clock is 120 seconds ahead finds that claim; a Stop hook in the main checkout holds its store and has read its ask ledger when a second Stop hook judges it stopped, its clock 120 seconds ahead of the first one's, or both clocks moved on 120 seconds while the first was held; rcf feedback submit in the main checkout has filed and recorded an issue for one entry and routes another to an outbox bundle when a worktree move takes the store and holds it past submit's wait; an earlier rcf feedback submit filed an issue and could not record it, and rcf feedback submit --dry-run runs; a Stop hook in the main checkout that judged a stopped move stopped was itself stopped (SIGKILL) inside its claim, and another Stop hook runs; or, with a main checkout whose .gitignore does not cover .rcf/feedback/ yet and a worktree that holds one pending entry, rcf feedback submit in the worktree files that entry while a Stop hook there holds the worktree's store past submit's wait, and the main checkout's .gitignore then gains .rcf/feedback/
acceptanceCriteria.when: rcf feedback add (no --force) records one entry from the worktree (in variant 2 this is the next rcf feedback command run there); in the base case and variant 2 the worktree is then removed with git worktree remove (no --force); in variant 5 rcf feedback list --all --json, rcf feedback hook stop --harness claude-code with a new session_id and rcf feedback add (no --force) are each run in the worktree, then the main checkout's .gitignore gains .rcf/feedback/, rcf feedback add records one entry from the worktree and the worktree is removed with git worktree remove (no --force); in variant 6 rcf feedback add (no --force) is run in the worktree; in variant 7 rcf feedback add (no --force) is run in the worktree, then the main checkout's state.json is made writable again, rcf feedback list --all --json is run in the worktree as the next command and the worktree is removed with git worktree remove (no --force); in variant 8 rcf feedback list --all --json is run in the worktree, then the worktree's outbox/ is made writable again, rcf feedback list --all --json is run in the worktree as the next command and the worktree is removed with git worktree remove (no --force); in variant 9 the commands run at the same time, then rcf feedback list --all --json is run in the worktree as the next command and the worktree is removed with git worktree remove (no --force); in variant 10 the commands run at the same time (the move held past the other commands' wait in one case, the move's process stopped, or started more than 60 seconds earlier and not refreshed since, in others), then rcf feedback list --all --json is run in the worktree as the next command and the worktree is removed with git worktree remove (no --force); in variant 11 rcf feedback add runs in the main checkout while that move is still running, then the move finishes, rcf feedback list --all --json is run in the worktree as the next command and the worktree is removed with git worktree remove (no --force); in variant 12 the commands run at the same time, then rcf feedback list --all --json is run in the worktree as the next command (after a submit, rcf feedback submit --yes runs once more in the main checkout first) and the worktree is removed with git worktree remove (no --force); in variant 13 the commands run at the same time, the first Stop hook let go before the second and each held command let go once the later one has run, then each Stop hook that exited 1 runs once more for its session; after a submit, rcf feedback submit --yes runs once more in the main checkout (and, in the worktree case, once rcf feedback list --all --json has run in the worktree, once in each checkout); then rcf feedback list --all --json is run in the worktree as the next command and the worktree is removed with git worktree remove (no --force)
acceptanceCriteria.then: rcf feedback list --json run from the main checkout lists that entry by id with status pending, and rcf feedback list there prints its id; in variant 2 rcf feedback list --all --json from the main checkout lists every entry the worktree held, the new entry and the main checkout's own, each id exactly once with the status it had (the discarded one stays discarded), and git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all there lists nothing under .rcf/feedback/; in variant 3 the add exits 2, stderr names .rcf/feedback, rcf doctor --fix and the main checkout's directory, nothing is created under either checkout's .rcf/feedback/, and git status in the main checkout lists nothing under .rcf/feedback/; in variant 4 git status in the main checkout lists nothing under .rcf/feedback/, and an entry the add accepts (exit 0) is listed pending from the worktree, while a refusal exits 2; in variant 5, before the main checkout ignores the store, rcf feedback list --all --json in the worktree lists both held entries with the status they had, the Stop hook exits 2 with the ask counting the held pending entry, the add exits 2 with stderr naming .rcf/feedback, rcf doctor --fix, the main checkout's directory and "the held entries move into the main checkout once it ignores .rcf/feedback/", the worktree's entries.jsonl is byte-identical, nothing is created under the main checkout's .rcf/feedback/ and git status there lists nothing under .rcf/feedback/; after the main checkout ignores the store the add exits 0 and, after git worktree remove, rcf feedback list --all --json from the main checkout lists both held entries and the new one, each id once with its status; in variant 6 the add exits non-zero, stderr names the error the move hit (EACCES) and the main checkout's directory, the worktree's .rcf/feedback/ is byte-identical to before (no new entry, nothing removed) and nothing is written under the main checkout's .rcf/feedback/; in variant 7 the add exits 1, stderr names the error the move hit (EACCES or permission denied) and the main checkout's directory, the worktree's .rcf/feedback/ is byte-identical to before (nothing written to its queue, nothing it held removed) and rcf feedback list --all --json from the main checkout lists its own entry and every held entry, each id exactly once with the status it had (the discarded one stays discarded); the next command exits 0 and leaves no held file under the worktree's .rcf/feedback/, git worktree remove (no --force) succeeds, rcf feedback list --all --json from the main checkout lists every id once with its status, each line the worktree held is in the main checkout's entries.jsonl exactly once, and git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all there lists nothing under .rcf/feedback/; in variant 8 the list exits 1, stderr names the error the move hit (EACCES or permission denied) and the main checkout's directory, every held file the command removed from the worktree has its content in the main store (each line of the held entries.jsonl is a line of the main checkout's entries.jsonl, every ask record of the held state.json is in the main checkout's state.json, a removed outbox bundle is byte-identical in the main checkout's outbox/), every held file still in the worktree is byte-identical, nothing new is written under the worktree's .rcf/feedback/, and rcf feedback list --all --json from the main checkout lists every held entry, each id exactly once with the status it had; the next command exits 0 and leaves no held file under the worktree's .rcf/feedback/, git worktree remove (no --force) succeeds, rcf feedback list --all --json from the main checkout lists every id once with its status, and git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all there lists nothing under .rcf/feedback/; in variant 9 each held bundle's bytes are in exactly one file of the main checkout's outbox, a main outbox file that was there before is byte-identical, each line of the held entries.jsonl is in the main checkout's entries.jsonl exactly once, each ask record of the held state.json is in the main checkout's state.json exactly once, a bundle written while the move ran is in exactly one file of the main checkout's outbox, an entry recorded while it ran is listed once with status pending, no held file is left under the worktree's .rcf/feedback/, rcf feedback list --all --json from the main checkout lists every id once with the status it had, git worktree remove (no --force) succeeds, and git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all there lists nothing under .rcf/feedback/; in variant 10 every ask record the main checkout's state.json held before and every ask record its Stop hook wrote while the move ran are in it exactly once, the Stop hook in a session that already asked exits 0 without asking, a writer held past its wait exits 1 with stderr naming the running command's process id and the main checkout's directory and writes nothing under the main checkout's .rcf/feedback/, rcf feedback add after a stopped move or past a move that started more than 60 seconds earlier and has not been refreshed since exits 0 and its entry is listed once with status pending, each held bundle, entries line and ask record is in the main checkout's store exactly once, no held file is left under the worktree's .rcf/feedback/, rcf feedback list --all --json from the main checkout lists every id once with the status it had, git worktree remove (no --force) succeeds, and git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all there lists nothing under .rcf/feedback/; in variant 11 the move still running is not taken for stopped: rcf feedback add exits 1 once its wait runs out, with stderr naming the running command's process id and the main checkout's directory, and writes nothing under the main checkout's .rcf/feedback/; afterwards each held bundle, entries line and ask record is in the main checkout's store exactly once, no held file is left under the worktree's .rcf/feedback/, rcf feedback list --all --json from the main checkout lists every id once with the status it had, and git worktree remove (no --force) succeeds; in variant 12 exactly one command goes on in the main checkout's store at any instant (no Stop hook completes its read and write while another is inside its own), each Stop hook exits 2 as it would alone and its ask record is in the main checkout's state.json exactly once; the reader of entries.jsonl reads only whole lines and lists every entry once with the status it had before or after the write; submit records the filing once the move lets the store go or has stopped refreshing (exit 0), or, held past its wait, exits 1 with stderr naming the filed issue's URL and the entry's id and never saying it wrote nothing, and the next submit does not file that entry again (each entry is filed exactly once) and it is listed with status submitted; the opted-out Stop hook exits as it would alone (exit 0, the same output), without waiting, and writes nothing under the main checkout's .rcf/feedback/; a writer held up by a record that cannot be parsed and is 30 seconds old exits 1 once its wait runs out, with stderr naming that file's path and its age, and writes nothing under the main checkout's .rcf/feedback/, and once that file is more than 60 seconds old rcf feedback add exits 0 and its entry is listed once with status pending; afterwards each held bundle, entries line and ask record is in the main checkout's store exactly once, no held file is left under the worktree's .rcf/feedback/, rcf feedback list --all --json from the main checkout lists every id once with the status it had, git worktree remove (no --force) succeeds, and git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all there lists nothing under .rcf/feedback/; in variant 13 the second Stop hook waits for the first, which it never sets aside while it runs (no Stop hook completes its read and write while the other is inside its own), each exits 2, and each one's ask record is in the main checkout's state.json exactly once; the Stop hook judged stopped writes nothing more once the later hook has taken the store, exits 1 with stderr naming the path of the record of its hold that it lost, the later hook's ask record is kept exactly once, and once it runs again its own ask record is there exactly once; the submit busy after its filing exits 1 with stderr naming the filed entry's id and the issue's URL and never saying it wrote nothing, and the next submit does not file that entry again; the dry run lists the entry already filed among none it would file, comment on or bundle and writes nothing under the main checkout's .rcf/feedback/; the claim the stopped Stop hook left is removed once the next Stop hook has gone on past it (exit 2); in the worktree case no held file is left under the worktree's .rcf/feedback/ once its queue has moved, the entry is filed exactly once across every submit, and it is listed once with status submitted;
